note: One plain-English description per log template, keyed by 'partition<TAB>template'. Written by an LLM that saw only the template and one example, never root_cause labels or eval queries. Review before committing; edit by hand if needed.

descriptions.ERROR|23505\tduplicate key value violate: Postgres unique constraint violation on the users email column. An insert or update tried to store an email that already exists, so the signup or account update fails with a duplicate key error.
descriptions.ERROR|23505\tUniqueViolation: Key (sku)=: Postgres unique violation on the product SKU. Creating or importing a product whose SKU already exists failed, so the create or import request is rejected as a duplicate key conflict.
descriptions.ERROR|40P01\tConcurrent updates to inven: Postgres deadlock caused by concurrent updates to the same inventory or stock row. One transaction was rolled back, so a stock reservation, order or inventory update may have failed.
descriptions.ERROR|40P01\tdeadlock detected: Process: Postgres deadlock detected. Two database processes were each waiting on locks the other held, so one transaction was aborted and its query failed with a lock conflict error.
descriptions.ERROR|40P01\tTransaction aborted due to: Postgres deadlock while updating an order. The database aborted the transaction and the application is retrying it, so order updates may be slow or fail once the retries run out.
descriptions.ERROR|57014\tcanceling statement due to: Postgres query canceled because it ran longer than the statement timeout. The slow, long-running SQL statement was killed, so the request that depended on it failed or returned an error.
descriptions.ERROR|CERT_HAS_EXPIRED\tError: certifica: TLS/SSL handshake failed because the remote server's certificate has expired. Secure connections to that service are rejected, so every call that depends on it fails until the certificate is renewed.
descriptions.ERROR|CERT_HAS_EXPIRED\tSSL certificate: Expired SSL/TLS certificate for an external API or third-party provider. Outbound HTTPS requests to that provider are being rejected, so features that rely on the integration are failing.
descriptions.ERROR|DISK_FULL\tDisk usage at <num>% on: Disk almost full on the data volume. The filesystem has run out of space and writes are failing, so the database, storage or service may reject requests or crash.
descriptions.ERROR|EAI_AGAIN\tDNS lookup for <host> f: Temporary DNS failure (EAI_AGAIN). The hostname lookup could not be resolved at the moment, so connections to that dependency fail until name resolution or the DNS resolver recovers.
descriptions.ERROR|ECONNREFUSED\tconnect ECONNREFUSED: TCP connection refused. Nothing is accepting connections at the target address and port, so the service cannot reach a dependency such as the database, cache or another backend, which may be down.
descriptions.ERROR|EDQUOT\tFailed to persist upload <: File upload failed because the storage volume's disk quota was exceeded. The uploaded file was not saved, so user uploads and attachments fail until space is freed or the quota is raised.
descriptions.ERROR|ENOSPC\tENOSPC: no space left on d: No space left on device (ENOSPC). The disk or filesystem is full, so file writes such as logs or data fail and the process may crash or lose output.
descriptions.ERROR|ENOTFOUND\tgetaddrinfo ENOTFOUND <: DNS lookup failed with ENOTFOUND. The hostname could not be resolved or does not exist, so outbound HTTP requests or service calls to that host fail completely.
descriptions.ERROR|ENOTFOUND\tUnable to resolve hostn: Hostname could not be resolved (DNS ENOTFOUND) while calling an external provider or internal dependency, so the outbound request failed and that integration is unavailable.
descriptions.ERROR|ETIMEDOUT\tConnection to postgres: Postgres connection timeout. The TCP connection to the database server did not complete in time, so the app cannot open a database connection and its queries or requests fail.
descriptions.ERROR|ETIMEDOUT\tCould not reach primary: Connections to the primary Postgres database kept timing out, and the application gave up after its retries. The database is unreachable, so queries and requests that need it fail.
descriptions.ERROR|HTTP_502\tPayment provider respond: Payment gateway or processor returned HTTP 502 Bad Gateway when creating a charge. This is an upstream provider error. The payment failed or its status is unknown, checkout may break, and retries could double charge.
descriptions.ERROR|HTTP_503\tStripe API request faile: Stripe payments API call failed with HTTP 503 Service Unavailable from upstream. The provider is unavailable or overloaded, so charges and payment processing may fail. Retry with backoff and check the Stripe status page.
descriptions.ERROR|HTTP_504\tGateway timeout (<num>): HTTP 504 gateway timeout from the payment provider while capturing an authorized payment intent. The upstream request timed out and capture status is uncertain, so funds may go uncollected or be captured twice on retry.
descriptions.ERROR|INVENTORY_NEGATIVE\tInventory for: Inventory stock level became negative after reserving items for an order. Stock counts are inconsistent, items may be oversold, orders may be unfulfillable, and warehouse quantities need reconciliation.
descriptions.ERROR|KNEX_TIMEOUT\tKnexTimeoutError: Kn: Knex query builder timed out waiting for a Postgres database connection. The connection pool is full or leaking, possibly from a query missing its transaction. Queries and API requests hang or fail.
descriptions.ERROR|NPE\tjava.lang.NullPointerExceptio: Java NullPointerException (NPE): code called a method on a null object reference. The backend service crashes on this path, requests fail with 500 internal server error, and an unchecked null value is involved.
descriptions.ERROR|OOM\tWorker process exceeded memor: Worker process used more memory than its configured limit and was killed and restarted. This is an OOM or high memory usage, possibly a leak. In-flight jobs are lost and a crash loop is possible.
descriptions.ERROR|OVERSOLD\tOversold product <id>: <: An order was accepted for more units than are in stock, so the product is oversold. The inventory stock check failed, and orders may be unfulfillable and need cancellation or refunds.
descriptions.ERROR|POOL_EXHAUSTED\tDatabase pool exha: Postgres database connection pool exhausted: all clients are busy and requests are queued waiting for a connection. Expect pool saturation, high latency, timeouts and failing API requests.
descriptions.ERROR|TypeError\tTypeError: Cannot read: JavaScript TypeError in Node.js: code read a property of undefined or null. A value is missing or unchecked, the code crashes, and the request fails with 500 internal server error.
descriptions.ERROR|UNHANDLED\tUnhandled exception: tr: Unhandled exception from accessing a property on an undefined object. This is an uncaught error in Node.js code from missing or unloaded data. The request crashes with a 500 error and the process may exit.
descriptions.ERROR|X509\tTLS handshake with <host> fa: TLS/SSL handshake to an external service failed because the x509 certificate is expired or not yet valid. The HTTPS connection fails certificate validation, so outbound integration calls fail. Check cert renewal or clock skew.
descriptions.FATAL|53100\tPANIC: could not write to f: Postgres PANIC: the disk is full, so the server cannot write the WAL (write-ahead log) file. The database crashes or shuts down, writes fail, and the outage lasts until disk space is freed.
descriptions.FATAL|53300\tFATAL: remaining connection: Postgres too many connections: max_connections is reached and the remaining slots are reserved for superusers. New database connections are rejected, the application cannot connect, and requests fail from connection exhaustion.
descriptions.FATAL|ERR_HEAP_OOM\tFATAL ERROR: Reached: Node.js process crashed with JavaScript heap out of memory after reaching the V8 heap limit. This is an OOM crash from a memory leak or large allocation. The service restarts, requests are dropped, check max-old-space-size.
descriptions.FATAL|OOM\tjava.lang.OutOfMemoryError: J: Java JVM ran out of heap memory (OutOfMemoryError, OOM). Garbage collection is under pressure from a possible memory leak or undersized -Xmx heap. The service may crash, hang or restart.
descriptions.FATAL|OOMKilled\tContainer <*> was OOMKi: Kubernetes container was killed by the kernel OOM killer for going over its memory limit (exit code 137). The pod restarts and may enter CrashLoopBackOff, and in-flight requests are lost.
descriptions.INFO|\tBatch of <num> messages processed: Message queue consumer processed a batch of messages from Kafka or a similar broker, reporting how many failed. Normal batch processing; nonzero failures mean some messages errored and may need retry or dead-lettering.
descriptions.INFO|\tCron <*> completed successfully: Scheduled cron job or periodic background task finished without errors. Normal maintenance run such as cleanup; confirms the scheduler triggered it and the job ran to completion.
descriptions.INFO|\tGET <*> <num> <num>ms: HTTP GET request access log line with the API route, response status code and latency in milliseconds. Normal read traffic, useful for tracking slow endpoints, response times and request volume.
descriptions.INFO|\tHandled <*> in <num> ms (status <: Normal HTTP request handled by the API server, logging the endpoint, response latency in milliseconds and HTTP status code. Useful for tracing slow responses, request timing and endpoint traffic.
descriptions.INFO|\tHealth check OK: Service health check endpoint responded successfully, meaning the application is alive and answering liveness probes from monitoring, a load balancer or Kubernetes. Normal heartbeat, no impact on traffic.
descriptions.INFO|\tIssued new access token for <id>,: Authentication service issued a new access token (JWT or bearer token) for a user, with its expiry time. Normal token generation or refresh after login, relevant for session and auth expiry issues.
descriptions.INFO|\tJob <*> finished in <num>ms, proc: Background job or batch worker run completed, reporting total execution time and number of items processed. Normal scheduled task completion, useful for tracking job duration, throughput and slow batch processing.
descriptions.INFO|\tLogin succeeded for <email> <*>: User authentication succeeded: an account signed in by email, with extra login details such as the MFA (multi-factor authentication) flag. Normal sign-in event, useful for auditing account access.
descriptions.INFO|\tPOST <*> <num> <num>ms: HTTP POST request access log line showing the API route, response status code and latency in milliseconds. Normal write request traffic, useful for spotting slow endpoints or error status codes.
descriptions.INFO|\tPUT <*> <num> <num>ms: HTTP PUT request access log line with the API route, response status code and latency in milliseconds. Normal update traffic, useful for spotting slow endpoints, failed updates or error responses.
descriptions.INFO|\treadiness probe passed (db=up, ca: Kubernetes readiness probe succeeded: service confirmed its Postgres database and Redis cache connections are up, so the pod can receive traffic. Normal healthy state, includes check latency.
descriptions.INFO|\trequest completed <*> status=<num: Structured access log for a completed HTTP request, with method, path, status code, duration and a request ID for correlation and distributed tracing. Normal API traffic, useful for latency analysis.
descriptions.INFO|\tService started on port <num> (ve: Application server process started up and is listening on its port, logging the deployed version. Normal startup after a deploy, restart or pod rescheduling; useful for tracking releases and crash loops.
descriptions.INFO|\tUser <id> logged in successfully: User authentication succeeded and the user logged in, recording the client IP address. Normal sign-in event, useful for security auditing, tracking account access and spotting logins from unusual locations.
descriptions.WARN|\tFailed to read session from cache: Session store read failed because the Redis cache client connection was closed. Users' sessions may not load, causing unexpected logouts or authentication failures; points to a dropped or lost Redis connection.
descriptions.WARN|\tMessage processing delayed <num>s: Queue consumer is falling behind: message processing lag keeps rising and the backlog is growing. Consumer lag on Kafka or message queue means delayed jobs, stale data and slow downstream processing.
descriptions.WARN|ECONNREFUSED\tCache unreachable at: Redis cache connection refused, cache is down or unreachable, so the service falls back to querying the Postgres database directly. Expect higher database load, slower responses and degraded performance until the cache recovers.
descriptions.WARN|ECONNRESET\tRedis connection lost (: Redis client lost its TCP connection (socket reset by peer) and is automatically reconnecting with backoff; cache reads, writes and sessions may fail or slow down until the connection comes back.
descriptions.WARN|EMAIL_TAKEN\tCannot create account:: Signup or registration was rejected because the email address already belongs to an existing user account. This is a duplicate email conflict and normal validation; the user sees an error and cannot sign up.
descriptions.WARN|HTTP_401\t<num> Unauthorized - sess: HTTP 401 Unauthorized: the user's login session is invalid, expired or revoked, so the request is rejected and the user is logged out and must sign in again. This is an authentication failure.
descriptions.WARN|HTTP_401\tRejected request to <*> a: API request rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized because the client's access or bearer token has expired. This is an authentication failure; the client must refresh the token or log in again before calls succeed.
descriptions.WARN|HTTP_429\t<num> Too Many Requests f: Our API rate limiter rejected an incoming client with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests for going over the per-minute request limit; that caller is throttled and its requests fail until the window resets.
descriptions.WARN|HTTP_429\tRate limit hit when calli: Outbound call to a third-party external API was throttled with HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; the service backs off and retries later, so dependent features or integration calls are delayed.
descriptions.WARN|HTTP_503\tCharge for order <id> fai: Payment charge failed because the payment processor or gateway is unavailable (HTTP 503 Service Unavailable). The checkout payment is not captured yet and will be retried, so the order stays pending.
descriptions.WARN|IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT\tIdempotency c: Duplicate order submission blocked by the idempotency key check; the same order request arrived twice, such as a retry or double click, and the repeat is rejected to prevent double charging.
descriptions.WARN|KAFKA_LAG\tConsumer group <*> lag i: High Kafka consumer group lag on a topic: many messages are waiting unconsumed behind the latest offsets. This growing queue backlog delays event processing and downstream updates.
descriptions.WARN|KAFKA_LAG\tKafka consumer is fallin: Kafka consumer lag is growing: the consumer is not keeping up and a backlog of unprocessed events is building, so downstream processing is delayed and data becomes stale.
descriptions.WARN|QUOTA_EXCEEDED\tThrottling tenant <: A tenant went over its per-minute API request quota and is being throttled by the multi-tenant rate limiter; that customer's excess requests are rejected or delayed, similar to HTTP 429.
descriptions.WARN|RECONCILE_MISMATCH\tStock reconcili: Inventory reconciliation found a stock count mismatch: the warehouse count differs from the expected system quantity. This inventory discrepancy can cause overselling, wrong availability or fulfillment problems.
descriptions.WARN|REDIS_LOADING\tReplyError: LOADING: Redis is still loading its dataset into memory from disk (RDB/AOF persistence) at startup or replica sync, so it rejects commands; cache and session operations fail until loading finishes.
descriptions.WARN|SLOW_QUERY\tDatabase call to <*> ex: Database query exceeded its time budget: a slow query or high latency in Postgres, so API endpoints that rely on that table respond slowly or may time out.
descriptions.WARN|SLOW_QUERY\tSlow query took <num>ms: Slow Postgres SQL query fetching a user's orders sorted by creation date took seconds. This is high database latency worth checking with EXPLAIN; order history pages and API responses become slow.
descriptions.WARN|TOKEN_EXPIRED\tBearer token rejecte: Authentication failed with HTTP 401 because the user's bearer JWT access token is expired (exp claim in the past); the request is rejected until the client refreshes the token or logs in again.
descriptions.WARN|TOKEN_EXPIRED\tTokenExpiredError: j: JWT verification failed with TokenExpiredError (jsonwebtoken library): the authentication token has expired, so the request is treated as unauthorized and the user must refresh the token or log in again.
